# core/der.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/der.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Reading ASN.1 DER, the encoding of X.509 certificates and
of most of what TLS carries (RFC 5280, ITU-T X.690).

What is proved: every access is in bounds, and an item `der_item` returns
lies inside the span it was asked to read: its content starts after the
tag and the length bytes and ends at or before the limit. The reader takes
what DER takes and nothing else: tags of one byte, definite lengths, and
the shortest form of every length. Not proved: that the bytes make a
valid certificate; that is for the layers above.

`import "core/der.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`der_item`](#der_item) | The element that starts at `at`, if the bytes `at..limit` of `b` begin with a well-formed one. |
| [`der_content_eq`](#der_content_eq) | The content of `it` holds exactly the bytes of `want` (the encoded value of an object identifier, say). |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `DerItem`

```bastio
struct DerItem { tag: u8, content: Span }
```

One element of DER: its tag byte and the span of its content.

## Functions

### `der_item`

```bastio
fn der_item(b: &Bytes, at: u64, limit: u64) -> Option[DerItem]
  requires limit <= blen(b) && at <= limit
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> at + 2 <= result.Some.content.start
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.content.start <= result.Some.content.end
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.content.end <= limit
```

The element that starts at `at`, if the bytes `at..limit` of `b` begin
with a well-formed one. The tag must be one byte (a tag number below 31),
the length definite and in its shortest form, and the content must fit
before `limit`. The next element starts at the end of the content.

Example:

```bastio
// SEQUENCE { INTEGER 5, OCTET STRING "hi" }
let mut b = balloc(9);
bset(&mut b, 0, 48);
bset(&mut b, 1, 7);
bset(&mut b, 2, 2);
bset(&mut b, 3, 1);
bset(&mut b, 4, 5);
bset(&mut b, 5, 4);
bset(&mut b, 6, 2);
bset(&mut b, 7, 104);
bset(&mut b, 8, 105);
let mut bad = 1;
match der_item(b, 0, blen(b)) {
  Option::Some(seq) => {
    if seq.tag == 48 && seq.content.start == 2 && seq.content.end == 9 {
      match der_item(b, seq.content.start, seq.content.end) {
        Option::Some(n) => {
          if n.tag == 2 && n.content.end - n.content.start == 1 { bad = 0; }
        },
        Option::None => {},
      }
    }
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(b);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `der_content_eq`

```bastio
fn der_content_eq(b: &Bytes, it: DerItem, want: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires span_in(it.content, b)
```

The content of `it` holds exactly the bytes of `want` (the encoded value
of an object identifier, say).

Example:

```bastio
let mut b = balloc(5);
bset(&mut b, 0, 6);
bset(&mut b, 1, 3);
bset(&mut b, 2, 85);
bset(&mut b, 3, 29);
bset(&mut b, 4, 15);
let mut want = balloc(3);
bset(&mut want, 0, 85);
bset(&mut want, 1, 29);
bset(&mut want, 2, 15);
let mut ok = false;
match der_item(b, 0, blen(b)) {
  Option::Some(oid) => { ok = der_content_eq(b, oid, want); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(want);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```
